question: When can failsafe be disabled during return to home on the Matrice 30T?

intake.focus: failsafe disable during return to home
intake.reason: Guidance on whether failsafe can be disabled during RTH and applicable procedures for Matrice 30T

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance indicates reestablishing control link when possible and to discontinue flight until inspection if synchronization or delay issues prevent control inputs. The DJI Matrice 30T manual notes that canceling RTH due to a warning can leave the Intelligent Battery with insufficient power to land safely, risking a crash. Incident reports: there are no usable evidence found in the approved collection for DJI Matrice 30T incident reports (unverified accounts). Main gap: there is no clear evidence on whether failsafe can be disabled during RTH or whether RC control is allowed when the RC signal is normal; the manuals describe other RC/landing behaviors only, leaving key questions open.

claims.text: FAA AC 107-2A states: 'Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft.' If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.
claims.quote: Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft.

claims.text: FAA AC 107-2A states: 'Discontinue flight and/or avoid further flight operations until further inspection and testing of the control link between the ground control unit and the aircraft' when control inputs are not synchronized or delayed.
claims.quote: Discontinue flight and/or avoid further flight operations until further inspection and testing of the control link between the ground control unit and the aircraft
conditions: Control inputs are not synchronized or delayed

claims.text: If RTH is canceled following the warning, the Intelligent Battery may not have enough power for the aircraft to land safely, which may lead to the aircraft crashing or being lost.
claims.quote: If RTH is canceled following the warning, the Intelligent Battery may not have enough power for the aircraft to land safely, which may lead to the aircraft crashing or being lost
